title: Hub-client preview resource resolution via service worker (epic)
description:
Long-term direction: replace the iframe post-processor's resource-rewriting passes (CSS data-URIs, image data-URIs, the disabled <script> inlining block) with a service worker scoped to /.quarto/project-artifacts/ and project-relative paths. The SW intercepts fetch events and serves from the VFS, giving us:

- Single resolution path shared between top-frame and iframe.
- No data-URI churn on every render (iframes routinely carry hundreds of KB of inline base64 stylesheets today).
- Clean answer for the in-project image redirection bug.
- Plausible path for executing real JS bundles in preview iframes (Bootstrap collapse, search, copy-button, etc.) once SW + sandbox + COEP/COOP are set up correctly.

NOT in scope: cross-doc link click → editor navigation (bd-lnd3). That's a DOM-event concern, not a fetch concern; about:srcdoc iframes drop link clicks silently regardless of network resolution. The click-interception path stays in iframePostProcessor.ts even after the SW arc lands.

Children candidates (file as separate issues when this epic gets traction):
- SW bootstrap + scope registration in hub-client.
- VFS → fetch handler.
- Migration of CSS resolution (remove data-URI rewrite from iframePostProcessor).
- Migration of image resolution (remove data-URI rewrite + fixes the in-project image redirect bug).
- JS bundle execution in preview iframes (subsumes bd-e7b7 native+incremental constraints).
- Sandbox / COEP / COOP setup as required.

Parent epic: bd-0tr6 (websites, since the immediate motivation is the website rendering pipeline, but the SW infrastructure is broadly useful).

title: Hub-client: active-page parse error renders as 'Project render produced no output for the active page'
description:
When a website document has a Pass-1 parse error AND it is the active page in hub-client, the preview overlay shows the literal string 'Project render produced no output for the active page' instead of the actual parse diagnostic.

Repro: examples/websites/08-hub-preview/about.qmd has an unescaped apostrophe (line 11, 'pages\\'') that the strict Q2 markdown parser rejects with [Q-2-10] Closed Quote Without Matching Open Quote. The CLI shows the full ariadne-style snippet via 'warning: profile-pass skipped about.qmd: ...'. Hub-client shows only the generic message.

Root cause (located): crates/wasm-quarto-hub-client/src/lib.rs:1374-1428 — render_project_active_page_to_response() checks summary.pass2_failures but never checks summary.pass1_failures. When the active page failed Pass-1, both summary.outputs and summary.pass2_failures are empty, so the L1393 fallback fires.

Fix: in the L1381 'no output' branch, look up summary.pass1_failures for an entry whose input matches the active path; if found, build a RenderResponse with success: false, error from the failure summary, and diagnostics: failure.diagnostics mapped to JsonDiagnostic.

title: qmd reader drops whitespace between code_span and html_element (issue #182)
description:
Reader silently drops leading/trailing whitespace on bare html_element nodes when they're converted to RawInline, so AST loses the Space between adjacent Code and RawInline siblings. Writer then collides backticks and round-trip fails to re-parse.

Reproduction, root cause, and recommended fix scope are documented in claude-notes/issue-reports/182/triage.md on branch issue-182 (worktree .worktrees/issue-182). Short version: the html_element visitor's anchor-shorthand branch already handles leading_ws/trailing_ws correctly by emitting adjacent Space inlines; the sibling RawInline branch in the same match arm does not. The fix mirrors that pattern.

Localized in crates/pampa/src/pandoc/treesitter.rs (html_element arm). TDD-first per crates/pampa/CLAUDE.md: add a roundtrip fixture and an AST assertion before changing code.
close_reason: Fixed in f2867bb1 on branch issue-182. Reader now emits leading/trailing Space inlines around RawInline when the html_element node carries surrounding whitespace, mirroring the anchor-shorthand branch in the same match arm.

title: Investigate tree-sitter grammar CRLF handling on Windows
description: Cargo xtask verify step 4 (tree-sitter test) fails 5/451 pipe-table tests on Windows but passes on ubuntu-latest CI. Surfaced during PR 109 Windows verification on 2026-04-24. Root cause is ambiguous between a test-corpus CRLF issue (Scenario A, .gitattributes fix) and a grammar CRLF-handling bug (Scenario B, grammar.js fix). Must investigate before remediating — fixing the test would mask a real Windows-user bug if Scenario B applies. See design for reproducer and both scenarios. Related to bd-tjbr (sibling Windows dev-ergonomics work). Target branch feature/dev-setup-improvements or its own branch.
design:
Failure mode. cd crates/tree-sitter-qmd/tree-sitter-markdown && tree-sitter test reports 451 parses, 446 successful, 5 failed on Windows. All 5 failures are pipe-table tests: Example 201 (GFM), Pipe table can precede content (two variants), Pipe table can follow content, Pipe table with blank-line caption. file test/corpus/pipe_table.txt shows CRLF line terminators (426 CR paired with 426 LF). git ls-files --eol confirms i/lf w/crlf — stored as LF in the index, materialized as CRLF on Windows checkout via core.autocrlf=true. Same mechanism caused the quarto-doctemplate failures catalogued in q2-windows-verify-tests memory note.

Scenario A — test-corpus CRLF. Grammar is CRLF-agnostic. Parse trees for LF and CRLF inputs are identical. Tests fail only because the corpus .txt file embeds both the input text AND the expected S-expression AST, and the expected AST was written assuming LF parse output. Remediation is a scoped .gitattributes entry: crates/tree-sitter-qmd/tree-sitter-markdown/test/corpus/*.txt eol=lf. One line, followed by git rm --cached then git checkout to normalize existing files. Real Windows user qmd content continues to parse correctly regardless of line endings.

Scenario B — grammar CRLF bug. Grammar does not treat carriage-return-linefeed as a block boundary where it should. Real Windows user qmd content with CRLF endings parses incorrectly — pipe tables do not detect captions as separate blocks, block boundaries drift. This is a user-facing bug; only a Windows contributor running pampa against CRLF content catches it. Remediation is in crates/tree-sitter-qmd/tree-sitter-markdown/grammar.js — typically adding carriage-return to newline character classes or the external scanner logic. .gitattributes would mask this bug instead of fixing it.

Reproducer. Two layers, both diagnostic. Layer 1 tests grammar.js directly via tree-sitter parse. Layer 2 tests the full pampa pipeline that real users hit. Fixtures are written into the tree-sitter-markdown directory so tree-sitter parse picks up the configured grammar without an init-config step.

Layer 1 (grammar.js):

printf 'before\r\n\r\n| a | b |\r\n|---|---|\r\n| 1 | 2 |\r\n\r\nafter\r\n' > crates/tree-sitter-qmd/tree-sitter-markdown/test-crlf.qmd
printf 'before\n\n| a | b |\n|---|---|\n| 1 | 2 |\n\nafter\n' > crates/tree-sitter-qmd/tree-sitter-markdown/test-lf.qmd
cd crates/tree-sitter-qmd/tree-sitter-markdown
tree-sitter parse test-crlf.qmd > test-crlf.parse
tree-sitter parse test-lf.qmd > test-lf.parse
diff test-crlf.parse test-lf.parse

Layer 2 (pampa end-to-end):

cargo run --quiet -p pampa --bin pampa -- crates/tree-sitter-qmd/tree-sitter-markdown/test-crlf.qmd > pampa-crlf.out
cargo run --quiet -p pampa --bin pampa -- crates/tree-sitter-qmd/tree-sitter-markdown/test-lf.qmd > pampa-lf.out
diff pampa-crlf.out pampa-lf.out

Notes on the prior reproducer in this design field. pampa has no parse subcommand — it is cargo run -p pampa --bin pampa -- input.qmd, with default -f markdown -t native. Git Bash /tmp resolves to %TEMP% but native Windows binaries resolve /tmp to C:\tmp\, so the previous version would have created files Git Bash could not find later. Use repo-local paths.

If both diffs are empty then Scenario A applies. If either diff is non-empty then Scenario B applies. Layer 2 also tells us whether the bug propagates past pampa's input handling into the Pandoc AST that real users render from.

Broader git cross-platform context. The 2026 consensus is that most projects do not need .gitattributes. core.autocrlf=true plus LF-tolerant tooling handles 99 percent of cross-platform cases. quarto-cli is an example — no .gitattributes and no CRLF-related failures. .gitattributes is for files that must be a specific line ending (shell scripts, batch files), binary files misdetected as text, and whitespace-sensitive test corpora where the consuming tool is itself correct. Over-restrictive patterns like * text=auto eol=lf force LF everywhere and are worse for cross-platform dev than no config. The target for this project is minimal, scoped .gitattributes only where the test harness cannot be fixed — and only in Scenario A.

Out of scope. Broader .gitattributes sweep for the whole repo. Fixing the 8 quarto-doctemplate CRLF failures already catalogued in q2-windows-verify-tests (separate work). Tree-sitter CLI changes (upstream, not ours).
acceptance_criteria: Reproducer runs and classifies failure as Scenario A or Scenario B. If Scenario A then .gitattributes entry added for test/corpus/*.txt and cargo xtask verify step 4 passes on Windows. If Scenario B then follow-up beads issue filed for grammar.js fix at higher priority and this investigation issue closes with evidence. q2-windows-verify-tests memory note updated with resolution and link to fix PR or follow-up issue. No regression in CI — tree-sitter tests continue to pass on Linux.
close_reason: Scenario B classified. Follow-up bd-0gsj filed at P1 for the grammar.js fix; full evidence in that issue's design and in the closing comment here.

comments.author: cderv
comments.text:
Investigation complete. Result: Scenario B (real grammar CRLF bug). Layer 1 (tree-sitter parse on grammar.js) showed pipe_table extents diverge between CRLF and LF inputs — CRLF case absorbs the trailing paragraph as a malformed table row. Layer 2 (cargo run -p pampa) confirmed pampa does not normalize line endings before parsing, so the bug propagates to the Pandoc AST that drives every output format. Real Windows users with default core.autocrlf=true and the common pattern of a pipe table followed by content render structurally wrong documents. .gitattributes alone would have masked this.

Follow-up filed at higher priority: bd-0gsj — Fix CRLF handling in tree-sitter-qmd grammar.js for pipe tables (P1, bug). Full evidence and reproducer carried over to bd-0gsj design field.

title: Audit listing config parsing for PandocInlines / yaml-markdown-syntax-error fallthrough
description:
Discovered while writing L5 (bd-5vsr) snapshot test #33. Quarto YAML often parses bare frontmatter strings as PandocInlines (e.g. when a glob like 'posts/*.qmd' confuses the markdown sublexer and lands as a Span carrying the 'yaml-markdown-syntax-error' class). 'parse_contents' (config.rs:572) was matching only Scalar/Glob/Array variants, so 'contents: "posts/*.qmd"' silently parsed as an empty Vec, and apply_type_defaults then injected the default '*.qmd' glob — making cross-directory listing globs invisible at runtime even though the unit tests passed.

Fix in L5: route 'parse_contents' through 'as_plain_text' first, mirroring 'parse_listings' top-level shorthand handling. Two new unit tests lock the behavior (contents_pandoc_inlines_string_parses_as_glob, contents_array_with_pandoc_inlines_items_parses).

Audit asks: what other listing-config parser branches in config.rs are still vulnerable to the same trap? Likely candidates from a quick read: parse_filter_list, parse_string_list, parse_sort, parse_field_types — any branch that matches on ConfigValueKind::Scalar(Yaml::String(_)) directly without a PandocInlines fallthrough should be reviewed and either rewritten to use as_plain_text first or have explicit PandocInlines handling added. Add unit-test coverage for each PandocInlines path discovered.

Out of scope but related: this is also a signal that the YAML parser's 'PandocInlines wrapping for any string with markdown-special chars' choice imposes a hidden tax on every config consumer in the tree. A broader design pass on whether such strings should be unwrapped before reaching consumers (or whether consumers should always use as_plain_text by convention) would be worth doing.

title: Fix Windows path-separator assumptions in pampa quarto_api path tests
description: On Windows, ~10 tests in crates/pampa/src/lua/quarto_api.rs (test_normalize_path_simple, test_normalize_path_with_dots, test_normalize_path_with_dotdot, test_normalize_path_with_dotdot_at_root, test_normalize_path_relative, test_normalize_path_relative_with_dotdot, test_quarto_utils_resolve_path_relative, test_quarto_utils_resolve_path_relative_with_subdir, test_quarto_utils_resolve_path_with_dotdot, test_script_dir_stack_resolve_path_uses_top) fail because expected paths are hardcoded with forward slashes ('/some/extension/dir/data.json') while the Windows implementation joins with backslashes via Path::join. Different category from bd-3pe8 (PR #95) which fixed Lua source-string path interpolation; these are output-comparison failures. Need to decide: (a) normalize quarto.utils.resolve_path output to forward slashes in production (matches quarto-cli pathWithForwardSlashes convention), or (b) write tests with platform-correct expectations using PathBuf::join. Surfaced 2026-04-28 while running cargo nextest -p pampa on Windows. Same set of tests run twice (library + bin/pampa integration), so 18-20 visible failures from one root cause.

title: Display math inside a blockquote retains '> ' continuation prefix in content (issue #181)
description:
Tree-sitter grammar rule `pandoc_display_math` (crates/tree-sitter-qmd/tree-sitter-markdown/grammar.js:367) matches its body as a single regex `/([^$]|[$][^$]|\\$)+/` between the two `$$` delimiters. When the math block is inside a blockquote, the interior `> ` block-continuation markers are never consumed by the grammar's `block_continuation` machinery; they end up verbatim inside the captured node text and then inside `Math.text` (see crates/pampa/src/pandoc/treesitter.rs:502-513). The qmd writer then correctly re-prefixes every line of the math body with `> ` when emitting it inside a blockquote, producing `> > p = q` and adding one more `> ` level on each round trip.

Fix is at the grammar level: make `pandoc_display_math` line-structured (loop over `$._newline | _math_line`) the way `pandoc_code_block` already is (grammar.js:828, with `_newline` consuming `block_continuation` at grammar.js:886). The writer is already correct; do not change it.

Triage doc and minimal repros live at claude-notes/issue-reports/181/ on branch issue-181. See triage.md there for full evidence including CST output and a contrasting fenced-code-in-blockquote case that parses cleanly.

title: Display math column-strip uses wrong column source, mishandles inline-wrapped and labeled math (issue #181 follow-up)
description:
Follow-up to bd-q6ed / issue #181, with revised diagnosis after a second-pass investigation (see `claude-notes/issue-reports/181/triage.md` § "Second-pass investigation").

## Symptom

Two reporter-supplied edge cases (rundel, 2026-05-12):

1. **Labeled display math inside a blockquote** — `> $$\n> p(x)\n> $$ {#eq-p}` round-trips with a literal `> ` left in `Math.text` after the second pass.
2. **Labeled display math at top level** — `$$\na\n  b\n$$ {#eq-x}` loses one column of leading whitespace from interior lines on each round trip.

Subsequent probing revealed both are instances of a broader brittleness in the column-strip introduced by bd-q6ed:

3. `_$$\na\n  b\n$$_` (emph wrapping multi-line displaymath) loses one space on **first** parse — no round trip needed.
4. `> _$$\n> a\n>   b\n> $$_` (same inside a blockquote) leaks `> ` AND loses interior whitespace on first parse.

## Root cause

`strip_continuation_prefix` in `crates/pampa/src/pandoc/treesitter.rs` uses `node.start_position().column` (the column of `$$`) as the strip width. That column equals the cumulative block-continuation prefix width **only when `$$` is the leftmost non-prefix character on its line**. Anything that precedes `$$` on the same line (`_`, `**`, `[`, the writer's own `[` for `quarto-math-with-attribute` Spans, etc.) shifts the column while the body bytes' source layout does not change. The strip then either eats real content (when the prefix is all whitespace/`>`) or refuses to strip real prefix (when the column overshoots into real content).

## Constraint

`DisplayMath` must remain an inline AST node — there are large existing corpora with display math nested inside paragraphs, and the grammar restructure proposed in the original triage would break those documents.

## Fix shape (reader-side, no grammar change, no AST shape change)

Change the strip-width source from `math_node.start_position().column` to the start column of the **enclosing block-leaf ancestor** (`pandoc_paragraph` / `pandoc_plain`). The cumulative block-continuation prefix width equals the paragraph's start column, which is constant across all interior lines of the paragraph regardless of what precedes `$$` on the opening line.

Pandoc's markdown reader uses this exact strategy (verified empirically). The fix matches Pandoc's behaviour on all probed cases — including lazy-continuation, nested blockquotes, list-item indent, and inline-wrapped multi-line math. The existing conservative `bytes ∈ {>, space, tab}` guard in the helper continues to handle lazy continuation correctly.

This single-input change subsumes:
- bd-q6ed canonical case (paragraph col = math col, identical result)
- bd-qpa2 edges A and B (paragraph col reflects true bq/top-level width)
- Inline-wrapped multi-line math at any block context

## Regression coverage to add

Fixtures under `crates/pampa/tests/roundtrip_tests/qmd-json-qmd/`:

- `labeled_display_math_in_blockquote.qmd` (bd-qpa2 edge A)
- `labeled_display_math_top_level_indented.qmd` (bd-qpa2 edge B)
- `emph_around_multiline_display_math.qmd`
- `emph_around_multiline_display_math_in_blockquote.qmd`

Reference inputs preserved at `claude-notes/issue-reports/181/exp-labeled-math-in-bq.qmd` and `exp-labeled-math-toplevel.qmd`.

## Worktree / branch

Implementation on its own branch with plan file at `claude-notes/plans/2026-05-12-displaymath-column-strip-fix.md`. Upstream: https://github.com/quarto-dev/q2/issues/181.

## Out of scope (separate issue if desired)

The writer's `[$$…$$]{attr}` emission for `quarto-math-with-attribute` Spans is suboptimal — Pandoc emits the natural form `$$\n…\n$$ {attr}` for the same AST. Switching to that form would improve readability and Pandoc compatibility, but with the reader fix above it is no longer required for round-trip correctness.

title: DocumentProfile: add includes: Vec<PathBuf> for incremental-rebuild invalidation
description:
Surfaced during the main -> feature/websites merge (bd-xfwx) that threaded IncludeExpansionStage before the DocumentProfile checkpoint.

Problem: after the merge, DocumentProfile.outline (and any other AST-derived fields) can be populated from headings / code / crossref targets spliced in via {{< include child.qmd >}}. The profile therefore depends on the contents of every included file, but the profile struct itself records no trail back to those files.

For incremental rebuilds (Phase 8 of the websites epic, bd-*) and for the future 'freeze' feature, the cache-key computation needs to invalidate a parent document's cached profile when ANY of its (transitive) includes change. Without tracking the include set on the profile, that is impossible.

Proposal: add a field roughly of the form

    includes: Vec<PathBuf>   // or Vec<IncludeEntry { path, hash }>

to DocumentProfile. Populated by IncludeExpansionStage (or by DocumentProfileStage reading a side-channel set that IncludeExpansionStage populated on the DocumentAst). Bump profile_version on the serialized shape.

Scope:
- Decide on the shape (bare PathBuf list vs. (path, content-hash) pairs). For Phase 8 we'll likely want the hash too so nav-state invalidation can compare without re-reading the files.
- Populate from IncludeExpansionStage.
- Extend contract doc (claude-notes/designs/document-profile-contract.md).
- Tests: profile records every included file (direct + transitive); round-trip serialization.

Non-blocking for the website-epic MVP; becomes a hard prerequisite for Phase 8.
close_reason: Closed as part of Phase 8.0 — DocumentProfile.includes added (v2). Verified by editing_include_invalidates_parent_profile (incremental_rebuild.rs).

title: Hub-client: parse error in another file is misattributed as 'Sidebar/Body link references unknown document'
description:
When a sibling page (e.g. about.qmd) fails Pass-1, opening a *different* page (e.g. index.qmd) shows two confusing warnings:
- 'Sidebar references unknown document about.qmd'
- 'Body link references unknown document about.qmd'

The file *exists*; it just failed to parse. The CLI also emits these warnings, but it additionally prints the underlying 'profile-pass skipped about.qmd: <diagnostic>' so a user can connect cause and effect. Hub-client never surfaces the Pass-1 failures at all — the diagnostics live on summary.pass1_failures[i].diagnostics and never cross the WASM boundary.

Root cause (located): crates/wasm-quarto-hub-client/src/lib.rs:1374-1428 ignores summary.pass1_failures entirely. The 'unknown document' warning itself is emitted at crates/quarto-core/src/transforms/navigation_href.rs:88-96 whenever ProjectIndex.get_profile(target) returns None.

Resolved fix shape (decisions D1, D2 in plan):
1. Add a dedicated 'pass1_failures' field to RenderResponse (per-entry { source_file, error, diagnostics }). Do NOT fold them into 'warnings'. Engine stays policy-free; consumers choose strict-vs-lenient (CLI: bd-creo; preview: this issue).
2. Add JsonDiagnostic.source_file: Option<String> so project-scoped warnings can be attributed.
3. PreviewErrorOverlay grows a section listing Pass-1 failures with source attribution and ariadne-style formatting.
4. navigation_href.rs wording change: 'references unknown document' → 'missing document information for' (proximal improvement; richer pass1-aware rewrite is a future task, not under this plan).

Plan: claude-notes/plans/2026-05-01-hub-client-website-render-ux.md (Bug 1 + decisions D1/D2).

Note: bd-mwtf (active-page case) is the narrower routing fix; bd-creo is the CLI-strictness sibling sharing the same wire-shape change.

title: q2-debug placeholder loses CustomNode type_name
description:
q2-debug's Block/Inline dispatchers (`hub-client/src/components/render/q2-debug/dispatchers.tsx`) currently render the miss path as `Not registered: CustomBlock` (or `
...
` for blocks) — using only `args.node.t`, which discards the CustomNode `type_name` discriminator. For CustomBlock / CustomInline AST nodes, the rendered debug placeholder should include the type_name so developers can see *which* CustomNode hit the fallback path. Example: `Not registered: CustomBlock(Callout)` instead of `Not registered: CustomBlock`. ~5 LOC change. Pattern: in the dispatcher, when `args.node.t === 'CustomBlock' || args.node.t === 'CustomInline'`, append the type_name to the displayed text. **Why**: q2-preview's parallel placeholder (`q2-preview/dispatchers.tsx` post-Plan-2C) already includes the tag name; q2-debug's debug-mode visualization should be at least as informative. **Discovered**: while reviewing Plan 2C (q2-preview customnode rendering, `claude-notes/plans/2026-05-09-q2-preview-plan-2c-customnode-rendering.md`). title: Improve cargo xtask dev-setup: cmake detection and xtask self-build lock
description: Two cross-platform dev-ergonomics improvements surfaced while verifying PR 109 on Windows after rebasing on main. Both are orthogonal to the WASM work and belong in their own PR. Target branch feature/dev-setup-improvements, worktree at .worktrees/dev-setup-improvements. Base branch origin/main. See design and acceptance fields for details.
design:
Background. Main added quarto-highlight (commit 1fa33da0, bd-n7x2 epic) which enables the `wasm` feature on tree-sitter for native builds. That pulls in wasmtime-c-api-impl as a transitive dependency, whose build.rs shells out to cmake. Result: cmake is now a hard prerequisite for `cargo build --workspace` on every platform. GitHub Actions runners have it pre-installed. Local dev boxes frequently do not (confirmed on Chris's Windows setup).

Fix 1 — check_cmake() in crates/xtask/src/dev_setup.rs. Follow the existing check_pandoc() pattern at line 155. Detection via `cmake --version`. If missing, print a warning with platform-specific install commands (scoop/winget on Windows, brew on macOS, apt/dnf on Linux). Unlike pandoc the warning should be stronger because cmake missing means `cargo build --workspace` fails, not just specific tests. No version constraint — any modern cmake works for wasmtime-c-api. Single function, no NativeTool struct abstraction (YAGNI).

Fix 2 — `--exclude xtask` in crates/xtask/src/verify.rs step 3. The current code at line 112 runs `cargo build --workspace`, which re-links target/debug/xtask.exe while the currently-running xtask.exe holds a file lock on Windows. Error: `failed to remove file ... Accès refusé (os error 5)`. Linux/macOS tolerate overwriting a running exe, so this was latent. Change to `["build", "--workspace", "--exclude", "xtask"]`. Step 5 (nextest) is unaffected — it compiles xtask as a test binary at a different path, no conflict. Cross-platform safe.

Fix 3 — CONTRIBUTING.md cmake subsection. Add after the existing "macOS: Homebrew LLVM (for WASM builds)" section. Same shape: one paragraph explaining why, then per-platform install commands. Covers Windows (scoop/winget), macOS (brew — note it bundles with Homebrew LLVM if already installed for WASM), Linux (apt/dnf).

Out of scope. Generic NativeTool struct for future deps. Version floor for cmake. Windows MSVC Build Tools check (Microsoft's canonical Rust-on-Windows guide already covers this).

Related. bd-jakt investigates a different cargo xtask dev-setup issue (--locked causing externref mismatch) — same file, different concern.
acceptance_criteria: check_cmake() runs in cargo xtask dev-setup and reports suitable version when cmake is on PATH. When cmake is absent, dev-setup prints a clear warning with platform-specific install commands but does not fail. cargo xtask verify succeeds on Windows without hitting the xtask.exe file lock. CONTRIBUTING.md lists cmake as a prereq with install commands for all three platforms. No regression in CI (xtask tests still run via step 5 nextest --workspace).
close_reason: Merged via PR #136

comments.text: PR opened: https://github.com/quarto-dev/q2/pull/136 (commits 32667694, d34da980). Leaving issue open until merge.

comments.author: cderv
comments.text:
Design rationale not captured above. The `wasm` feature on tree-sitter exists for runtime loading of user-defined tree-sitter grammars compiled to WASM, on the native side, via wasmtime-c-api. The 12 statically-linked grammars in quarto-highlight (python, R, JS, etc.) do not need it. Browser side uses a different mechanism (web-tree-sitter via wasm-bindgen, Phase 4). Source: crates/quarto-highlight/Cargo.toml:39-45. Already scoped to non-wasm32 targets, so the WASM build itself does not pay the cmake cost.

Can we avoid cmake entirely while keeping native runtime user-grammar loading via WASM? Not today. Tree-sitter 0.25 exposes one WASM-runtime feature: `wasm` -> `wasmtime-c-api` -> `wasmtime-c-api-impl` (the cmake-shelling-out crate). No alternative for wasmer, wasmi, or pure-Rust wasmtime. The choice is hard-wired into tree-sitter's C layer (lib/src/wasm_store.c), not just the Rust bindings, so a Cargo-feature-only fix is impossible. Upstream issue tree-sitter/tree-sitter#4715 ("Consider supporting wasm-c-api") was closed without action; no upstream issue or PR for pure-Rust wasmtime. No third-party fork solves this for the WASM-loading path.

Options.

(1) Contribute upstream pluggable WASM-runtime support or a pure-Rust wasmtime switch. Long path, depends on maintainers.

(2) Feature-gate the `wasm` activation in quarto-highlight (e.g. default-on `user-grammars` feature) so devs without cmake can opt out via `--no-default-features` and lose only runtime custom-grammar loading. Does not avoid cmake for the default build.

(3) Switch native runtime grammar loading from WASM to native shared libraries (.so / .dylib / .dll) using upstream's own `tree-sitter-loader` crate (crates/loader/ in tree-sitter/tree-sitter, published on crates.io). It uses `libloading` for dlopen / LoadLibrary and the `cc` crate to compile grammars to dylibs — only a C compiler, no cmake. This is the same path the `tree-sitter` CLI uses for `tree-sitter parse`. Trade-off: users distribute native dylibs per-platform instead of one portable .wasm.

PR 136 documented and detected cmake without exploring (1)-(3). The trade-off belongs with the lead dev who introduced quarto-highlight in bd-n7x2.

title: qmd parser/writer: round-trip `Str "@{some-key}"` (inline brace forms unsupported)
description:
Discovered while implementing bd-21gu. The qmd parser rejects bare `{...}` and `\\@{...}` in inline contexts:

  printf 'foo {some-key} bar\n' | cargo run --bin pampa -- -t native
  → Parse error (column 6, '{')
  printf '\\@{some-key}\n' | cargo run --bin pampa -- -t native
  → Parse error

This means a `Str` whose body contains `@{some-key}` (e.g. coming in via JSON) cannot be round-tripped, even though the writer-side `@` escape (bd-21gu) lookahead does include `{` so it would emit `\\@{some-key}` — the resulting qmd then fails to re-parse.

Two possible fixes (require investigation):
  1. Parser: accept bare `{...}` as a literal (inline-brace context disambiguation).
  2. Writer: escape `{` and `}` defensively for `Str` inlines (parallel to the @ fix).

Defer until needed by a real-world case.

title: hub-client e2e fails: @quarto/quarto-sync-client/dist/index.js not resolvable
description:
Running cargo xtask verify --e2e (or npm run test:all from hub-client) breaks Playwright with: 'Cannot find module .../node_modules/@quarto/quarto-sync-client/dist/index.js imported from hub-client/e2e/helpers/projectFactory.ts'.

quarto-sync-client's package.json declares main: dist/index.js, but dist/ is not built as part of npm install — only the source/import/types entries (pointing at src/) get used by Vitest. Playwright runs the helper in a plain Node process that uses the default resolver, which falls back to main.

Reproduces on:
- this branch (feature/q2-preview-command @ 63e27e8c)
- main @ d0d5d39e (i.e. pre-existing, not introduced by the q2-preview work)

Likely fix shapes:
1. Add a workspace-wide pre-step that builds quarto-sync-client's dist/ (mirror of how WASM is built via 'npm run build:wasm').
2. Switch hub-client's e2e helpers to import via a path that hits the source condition (loader / tsx / different resolver).
3. Set 'imports' / 'exports' on quarto-sync-client so the default Node resolver finds .ts via source.

Discovered while wiring q2-preview-spa's own Playwright suite into 'cargo xtask verify --e2e' (bd-vpsy / Phase A.7); the q2-preview-spa suite is unaffected because it doesn't import quarto-sync-client at all.

title: pampa: wire Meta and Pandoc filter callbacks in typewise dispatch
description:
Discovered while testing bd-o8pr Phase 3 (Lua filter resource channel).

pampa::lua::filter::filter_names lists 'Pandoc', 'Doc', 'Meta', 'Block', 'Blocks', 'Inline', 'Inlines' as recognized filter handler names — they get copied from globals into the filter table. But the typewise traversal in apply_typewise_filter does not actually invoke them.

This means a Lua filter that does:
  function Meta(meta) ... end
or:
  function Pandoc(doc) ... end

is silently ignored. Para/Str/Header/etc. all work.

This blocks:
- Lua-filter tests for the bd-o8pr 'additivity defense' (filter mutates meta.resources): the unit test in resource_report.rs covers the logic, but an E2E test through q2 render needs Meta callback support.
- General pandoc filter compatibility: many real filters do all their work in Pandoc(doc) or Meta(meta).

References:
- crates/pampa/src/lua/filter.rs:308 (filter_names list)
- crates/pampa/src/lua/filter.rs:1730 (apply_typewise_filter)
- crates/quarto-core/tests/project_resources.rs (filter_removing_meta_resources_does_not_drop_author_declaration test note)

title: tree-sitter qmd: multi-line block quote inside list item fails to parse
description:
Minimal repro:
```
- > a
  > b
```

Pandoc parses this as BulletList[[BlockQuote[Para[Str "a", SoftBreak, Str "b"]]]]. Our parser fails with a parse error at line 2 col 6.

Root cause: in crates/tree-sitter-qmd/tree-sitter-markdown/src/scanner.c, the LIST_ITEM match() function has a newline branch (line 537-540) that returns 2, causing match_line case 2 (line 1991-1996) to advance past the trailing \n of a content line. When STATE_MATCHING is left set after a SOFT_LINE_ENDING and the next scan() runs at end-of-line-2, this consumes the \n that the line-ending gate (line 2233) needs, breaking the parse.

BLOCK_QUOTE match() has no newline branch and does not advance, which is why bq-in-bq (`> > a\n> > b\n`) works but bq-in-list-item does not.

Affects all list markers: -, *, +, 1., 1), (1), (#).

Plan: claude-notes/plans/2026-05-11-bq-multiline-in-list-item.md

Approach (option 2 from the analysis): guard STATE_MATCHING re-entry so that when STATE_WAS_SOFT_LINE_BREAK is set and lookahead is \n/\r/EOF, we skip the match_line pass and let the line-ending gate handle it.

TDD: failing corpus tests first.

title: Eliminate serde_json::Value intermediate in pampa JSON writer
description: Native profile of parse_qmd_to_ast (the hub-client's entry) on scaled lorem-ipsum fixtures shows ~50-55% of runtime in memory movement (_platform_memmove) + allocator work, and ~5-7% in indexmap::Core::insert_full. title: Tree-sitter scanner over-eagerly excludes *, -, +, #, digits from soft-break
description:
The same class of bug as bd-af1e affects 5 more characters. The scanner's line-break handler at scanner.c:2286-2291 and 2371-2376 excludes these from soft-line-break candidates whenever they appear at the start of a continuation line:
- '*' (could be emphasis, list, thematic break)
- '-' (could be list, thematic break, setext header)
- '+' (could be list)
- '#' (could be ATX header)
- digits 0-9 (could be ordered list)

But each of these only opens a block in specific contexts (most need a trailing space, '#' needs space, '*'/'-'/'+' need space for list, '***'/'---' need 3+ for thematic break, digits need '.' or ')' followed by space). A bare 'X' followed by content is just inline text and should soft-break.

Verified pampa vs pandoc divergence on:
  foo bar
  *emph* baz                 → pampa splits, pandoc soft-breaks
  -text more                 → pampa splits, pandoc soft-breaks
  +text more                 → pampa splits, pandoc soft-breaks
  #hashtag more              → pampa splits, pandoc soft-breaks
  123abc more                → pampa splits, pandoc soft-breaks

Correct exclusions (pampa already matches pandoc for):
  * list item                → BulletList opens (correct)
  - list item                → BulletList opens (correct)
  # heading                  → Header opens (correct)
  1. item                    → OrderedList opens (correct)

Fix approach: same as bd-af1e (peek-count). For each char, peek the trailing context to decide if it actually opens a block:
- '*', '-': count run; if >=3 with all whitespace/eol after, thematic break (interrupt). If '* ' or '*\t', list (interrupt). Otherwise inline.
- '+': only list if followed by whitespace.
- '#': only ATX if followed by whitespace or eol.
- digits: only ordered list if followed by '.' or ')' AND space.

':' (fenced div / definition list) was excluded from this issue because its semantics are more entangled with qmd-specific features and pandoc-mode-specific rules — file separately if regression observed.

Sibling of bd-af1e. See claude-notes/plans/2026-04-30-tree-sitter-backtick-paragraph-split.md for the bd-af1e implementation pattern.
close_reason: Re-scoped: see bd-wv4e replacement for asterisks-only fix. The other characters (-, +, #, digits, :) have a backslash-escape workaround (\-text, \#hashtag, etc.) so are not severe enough to fix in this pass.

title: Optional-variable syntax: $variable?$ shorthand for $if(variable)$$variable$$endif$
description:
When users see Q-10-2 warnings on a variable they intend to be optional, today they have to wrap each reference in $if(variable)$$variable$$endif$. A short $variable?$ form would be cleaner and let authors silence the warning at the use site.

Feasibility (recorded in bd-xdnk plan §Follow-up):
- `?` is unused as a sigil in the current grammar.
- Doesn't collide with any pipe name (`pairs|first|last|rest|allbutlast|uppercase|lowercase|length|reverse|chomp|nowrap|alpha|roman|left|center|right`).
- Pipes already use `/` as separator (`tree-sitter-doctemplate/grammar/grammar.js:84-86`), so `?` doesn't conflict.
- Implementation cost: one grammar token, one `bool optional` field on `VariableRef`, one branch in `render_variable` that returns `Doc::Empty` silently when `optional` is set and the lookup fails.

Open question: should `?` propagate to applied partials (`$var?:partial()$`)? Probably yes — same intent. Not applicable to `$if$` itself.

Discovered while wiring template diagnostics through quarto render (bd-xdnk). Now that template warnings are user-visible, having a clean opt-out becomes more valuable.

title: Share link project never joins synced project set
description:
Visiting #/share/<indexDocId> opens the project but never adds it to the user's synced project set (profile doc). Later trying to add the same docId via the Connect form fails with a misleading 'may already exist' error.

Root cause is three separate bugs:
1. App.tsx share route gates projectSetActions.addProject on status === 'connected', which is racy against useProjectSet's async init. On initial share-link load the guard almost always fails, the add is skipped, and there is no retry.
2. ProjectSelector renders the list from projectSetEntries when useProjectSet is true, so the share-flow's IDB-only entry is invisible.
3. ProjectSelector.handleConnectProject skips the getProjectByIndexDocId dedupe check that the share route has, and projectStorage.addProject then collides with the IDB unique index on indexDocId. The form also never calls projectSetActions.addProject, so even a successful add wouldn't reach the synced set.

Full analysis and TDD fix plan in claude-notes/plans/2026-04-16-share-link-project-not-added.md.

Repro: https://quarto-hub.com/#/share/SNHcgVzUkWpGFmcxkCkpCDfFtmu?server=wss%3A%2F%2Fquarto-hub.com%2Fws&file=%2Felliot%2Findex.qmd&name=Demo+Playground — opens fine but SNHcgVzUkWpGFmcxkCkpCDfFtmu is absent from the reporting user's profile projects map, and manual add via Connect form fails with 'Failed to add project. The document ID may already exist.'

title: QMD writer drops shortcode arguments and delimiters
description:
User-reported round-trip failure: `printf '{{< video https://youtu.be/abc width="800" height="450" >}}\n' | pampa -t qmd` produces `{{video}}` — losing the `{{<` / `>}}` delimiters, the URL positional arg, and named keyword args.

Root cause: `crates/pampa/src/writers/qmd.rs:1716` `write_shortcode` emits only `{{ + name + }}`, ignoring `is_escaped`, `positional_args`, and `keyword_args`. Even the no-arg form is wrong (qmd syntax requires `{{< name >}}`, not `{{name}}`).

The parser populates the `Shortcode` struct correctly; the JSON / native writers preserve all data via `shortcode_to_span`. Only the qmd writer is broken.

The existing roundtrip suite in `tests/roundtrip_tests/qmd-json-qmd/` does NOT catch this: it goes qmd → JSON → qmd, and the JSON writer converts `Inline::Shortcode` to `Inline::Span`, so `write_shortcode` is never exercised.

Plan: claude-notes/plans/2026-04-30-shortcode-qmd-roundtrip.md
close_reason: Implemented qmd writer round-trip for shortcodes; switched keyword_args to LinkedHashMap for source-order preservation. End-to-end verified, full xtask verify green.

title: Suppress noisy 'lua error' panic stack traces in WASM (cosmetic — caught control flow)
description:
rust_lua_throw at crates/wasm-quarto-hub-client/src/c_shim.rs:452 panics with 'lua error' as a replacement for Lua's longjmp-based LUAI_THROW. The panics are caught by rust_lua_protected_call (catch_unwind) — this is expected control flow, not a bug. However, console_error_panic_hook prints the full stack trace for every panic, spamming both 'cargo xtask verify' output and hub-client production console (visible to users in browser).

Fix: install a custom panic hook that suppresses panics matching the Lua throw sentinel, while preserving full stack traces for genuine panics.

The hub-client e2e test helper already explicitly tolerates these as transient (hub-client/e2e/helpers/previewExtraction.ts:38-45).

title: Phase 9 follow-up: parallel Pass-1 over project files
description:
On a _quarto.yml edit, the Phase-8 cache-key invalidation propagates to every profile entry simultaneously. The orchestrator's pass_one loop (crates/quarto-core/src/project/orchestrator.rs) is sequential: it runs N head pipelines back-to-back. Trivially parallelizable since per-file work is independent.

Native: rayon + pollster-per-worker (matches the rest of the pipeline's Send-free trait shape). WASM: futures::future::join_all over the WasmRuntime calls.

Phase 9 plan §Risks calls this out — order-of-seconds latency on a 100-file project after a _quarto.yml edit. Active page render still feels snappy on warm-cache edits; this is the genuine cold-path.

title: Table caption parsing fails without blank line before caption
description:
Table captions using the colon syntax require a blank line before the caption line, but Pandoc doesn't require this. Example that fails: '| Header |
|--------|
| Data   |
: Caption'. Works with blank line: '| Header |
|--------|
| Data   |

: Caption'. This is a parser-level issue in the tree-sitter grammar or processing.
notes:
ROOT CAUSE IDENTIFIED:

The caption rule in grammar.js:257 requires $._blank_line as first element. When no blank line precedes ': Caption', the pipe table parser treats ':' as valid punctuation in cell contents, creating an extra table row instead of a caption.

KEY INSIGHT: In qmd, ': ' at line start is ONLY used for captions (no definition lists). This means zero ambiguity - we can safely recognize captions without requiring blank lines.

SOLUTION: Two-part fix:
1. Remove blank line requirement from caption grammar rule
2. Modify external scanner to terminate pipe tables when next line starts with ': ' (single colon for caption, not '::' for fenced div)

See detailed plan: claude-notes/plans/2025-10-27-table-caption-blank-line-fix.md

title: Redesign validation error architecture to match quarto-markdown-pandoc
description:
Redesign validation error structs to separate error data from presentation, following quarto-markdown-pandoc's architecture.

**Current problem**:
- ValidationError → DiagnosticMessage conversion loses machine-readable structure
- JSON output is just rendered DiagnosticMessage, not purpose-built
- Missing: full source ranges, schema paths, instance paths in structured format

**Goal**:
- Validator returns rich error struct with all information
- Error struct can be rendered for humans (ariadne) or machines (JSON)
- JSON output has full source ranges, paths, filenames in machine-readable format

**Study**: Compare quarto-markdown-pandoc error architecture with validate-yaml
**Output**: Written plan with proposed design
notes:
**Updated Plan (v2)**: See claude-notes/plans/2025-10-27-k-259-validation-error-architecture-redesign-v2.md

**Key Changes from v1**:
1. ✅ Use wrapper type (ValidationDiagnostic) instead of metadata field
2. ✅ Use filename strings instead of file_id numbers
3. ✅ Full SourceRange with start/end offsets + line/column

**Architecture**:
- Create ValidationDiagnostic wrapper type in quarto-yaml-validation
- Wraps DiagnosticMessage for text rendering
- Custom to_json() with purpose-built structure
- SourceRange has filename + full range info

**Benefits**:
- Type-safe (no Option, no pattern matching)
- Clean separation (DiagnosticMessage stays generic)
- Filename-based JSON (no file registry needed)
- Custom JSON tailored for validation
- Extensible (other diagnostics can follow same pattern)

**Timeline**: 6-9 hours (3-4h diagnostic + 1-2h binary + 2-3h testing)

**Next**: Review v2 plan and start implementation

title: Parser fails to recognize horizontal rules (---) in qmd files

The qmd parser is not correctly parsing horizontal rules (---). They appear to be getting confused with YAML metadata delimiters. When parsing a file with --- horizontal rules, they are completely omitted from the AST.

Test case in test-fixtures/horizontal-rule.qmd shows the issue - only 2 paragraphs are parsed instead of 3 paragraphs with 2 horizontal rules between them.

This needs investigation in the tree-sitter grammar or block parser logic.

title: Implement smart terminal color detection using OSC 10/11 queries
description:
Terminals support querying their current foreground/background colors using OSC 10/11 escape sequences. This could enable smart color selection in the ANSI writer.

Implementation would:
- Query terminal colors using \x1b]10;?\x1b\ and \x1b]11;?\x1b\
- Parse RGB response format (rgb:RRRR/GGGG/BBBB)
- Detect dark vs light backgrounds
- Adapt color palette for better contrast
- Fall back to current defaults if query fails

Challenges:
- Requires raw terminal mode
- Not available in pipes/redirects
- Adds complexity and latency
- Should be behind feature flag

See claude-notes/terminal-color-querying.md for detailed research and implementation notes.

title: Fix backslash escape handling in pandoc_str
description:

**Current behavior**:
Input: hello\*world
Our output: Str "hello\\*world" (backslash preserved)
Pandoc output: Str "hello*world" (backslash consumed)

**Root cause**:
The tree-sitter grammar captures backslashes as part of pandoc_str (see regex with \\. at tree-sitter-markdown/grammar.js:531). They need post-processing to convert escape sequences to literal characters.

**Investigation needed**:
- Determine if backslashes should be in separate backslash_escape nodes or handled within pandoc_str
- Check if the grammar needs changes or just the handler logic
- Add comprehensive tests for all escapable characters

**Context**: Discovered during tree-sitter refactoring (k-274). See also: claude-notes/plans/2025-10-31-tree-sitter-qmd-cleanup-completion.md which mentions this as future work.

**Estimate**: 2-3 hours (investigation + fix + tests)

  - pandoc_str (heading text)

**Handler needs to**:
1. Extract heading level from marker (atx_h1_marker through atx_h6_marker)
2. Process inline content (children between marker and end)
3. Handle optional attribute specifier
4. Return Pandoc Header block

title: Fix citation whitespace handling - leading space should be Space node, not in Str content
description:
Citations currently include leading whitespace in their content Str instead of creating a separate Space node.

**Current behavior**:
- 'Hi @cite' produces: [Str "Hi", Cite [...] [Str " @cite"]]
  Note the leading space in " @cite"
- 'Hi@cite' produces: [Str "Hi", Cite [...] [Str "@cite"]]

**Expected behavior**:
- 'Hi @cite' should produce: [Str "Hi", Space, Cite [...] [Str "@cite"]]
- 'Hi@cite' should produce: [Str "Hi", Cite [...] [Str "@cite"]]

**Root cause**:
The citation handler in treesitter.rs uses node_text() which includes leading whitespace from the tree-sitter node. Similar to inline_note_reference, citations need to detect leading whitespace and inject a Space node.

**Location**: 
- Handler: crates/quarto-markdown-pandoc/src/pandoc/treesitter.rs:727-730
- Helper: crates/quarto-markdown-pandoc/src/pandoc/treesitter_utils/citation.rs

**Solution approach**:
Similar to the inline_note_reference fix, check if the node text starts with whitespace and return IntermediateInlines with [Space, Cite] instead of just IntermediateInline(Cite).

**Related**: Same issue exists in inline_note_reference (currently being fixed).

title: Define CommonMark-compatible subset of qmd grammar
description:
Design and implement a formal subset of quarto-markdown that guarantees output compatibility with CommonMark 0.31.2. See claude-notes/plans/2025-11-06-commonmark-compatible-subset.md for full design.

Goals:
- 100% CommonMark spec test compliance (652 tests)
- Validation tooling (--strict-commonmark flag)
- Clear documentation of in/out features
- Differential testing against reference implementation

Rationale: Provides migration confidence, testing foundation, and interoperability guarantees. CommonMark chosen over Pandoc because it's stable, formally specified, and testable.
notes:
REVISED PLAN - see claude-notes/plans/2025-11-06-commonmark-compatible-subset.md

KEY INSIGHT: CommonMark spec only defines HTML output, not AST. We need to be precise about what we promise.

REFERENCE IMPLEMENTATION: comrak (Rust CommonMark parser)
- **Full compliance**: Passes 652/652 CommonMark 0.31.2 spec tests
- **Critical**: Must configure for CommonMark-only mode (disable GFM extensions)
- See claude-notes/plans/2025-11-06-comrak-ast-structure.md for detailed AST analysis

APPROACH: Whitelist subset where qmd_subset ⊂ qmd AND qmd_subset ⊂ CommonMark

INCLUDED: ATX headings, fenced code, emphasis/strong, inline links, lists, blockquotes, hr
EXCLUDED: qmd features (divs, callouts), edge cases (Setext, indented code, HTML, reference links)

SEMANTIC GRAMMAR: Define subset in terms of abstract semantic structure (Document, Block, Inline, etc.)
- Level 3: Abstract semantic structure (what we promise)
- Level 4: Pandoc AST (how we verify - secondary test)
- Level 5: HTML output (primary test - matches CommonMark spec)
- Level 2: Tree-sitter CST (implementation detail - NOT what we promise)

TESTING: 
- Primary: HTML output comparison (comrak HTML vs qmd HTML)
- Secondary: Pandoc AST equivalence (comrak → HTML → Pandoc vs qmd → Pandoc)
- Both using comrak configured for pure CommonMark (no GFM)

VALIDATION: --validate-subset flag + tree-sitter queries

ESTIMATE: 6-9 weeks over 4 phases

title: Add qmd-syntax-helper conversion rule for Q-2-10 apostrophe errors
description:
Now that we have comprehensive Q-2-10 error detection for apostrophes being misinterpreted as quote closes (covering 17 inline construct types), add an automatic conversion rule in qmd-syntax-helper to fix these errors.

**Error Pattern**: Q-2-10 "Closed Quote Without Matching Open Quote"
- Occurs when apostrophe followed by space is interpreted as closing single quote
- Example: `**Humans' Conceptions**` triggers error at the apostrophe

**Fix Strategy**: Escape the apostrophe with backslash
- Input: `a' b.` → Output: `a\' b.`
- Input: `**Humans' Conceptions**` → Output: `**Humans\' Conceptions**`

**Coverage**: Works across all inline constructs (17 types):
- Plain text, bold, emphasis, links, images, quotes
- Superscript, subscript, strikeout
- Editorial marks (insert, delete, edit comment, highlight)
- Inline footnotes, headings
- Both star and underscore variants

**Implementation**:
1. Detect Q-2-10 error code in parser output
2. Extract error location from error message
3. Insert backslash before the apostrophe at that location
4. Preserve all other formatting

**Testing**:
- Test with all 17 error corpus examples (010.qmd through 026.qmd)
- Verify fixed output parses cleanly
- Verify formatting is preserved (especially in nested constructs)

**Reference**: Error corpus examples in resources/error-corpus/010-026.qmd

title: Add error diagnostic for indented footnote content

The parser currently emits generic 'Parse error: unexpected character or token here'.

1. Detects footnote definitions followed by indented content

title: Fix parser handling of multi-byte emoji characters
description:
The tree-sitter grammar fails to parse multi-byte emoji characters (particularly numbered emojis like 1️⃣, 2️⃣, 3️⃣).

**Minimal reproduction**:
```markdown
::: {.content-visible when-profile="fr"}
1️⃣ Trouver le tableau
:::
```

**Error**: 'Parse error: unexpected character or token here' at the emoji position

**Technical details**:
- Emoji like 1️⃣ is a multi-byte UTF-8 sequence:
  - Digit '1' (U+0031): `31`
  - Variation Selector-16 (U+FE0F): `efb88f`
  - Combining Enclosing Keycap (U+20E3): `e283a3`
- Simplified emoji test cases parse correctly
- Error only occurs in real corpus files with complex context
- Likely issue with tree-sitter grammar's UTF-8 handling in certain states

**Files affected in lino-galiana corpus**:
- 04_webscraping/_exo1_solution.qmd (23 errors)
- 04_webscraping/_exo2b_suite.qmd (2 errors)
- git/exogit.qmd (4 errors)

**Impact**: ~29+ errors across 3+ files

**Priority**: High - this is the highest impact uncoded error pattern

See: claude-notes/investigations/2025-11-20-lino-galiana-uncoded-errors.md

title: Implement basic template evaluator
description:
Implement the basic template evaluation engine in src/evaluator.rs.

Initial scope (no pipes, no partials):
- Literal nodes -> output as-is
- Variable interpolation -> resolve from context, render value
- Conditionals -> evaluate truthiness, render appropriate branch
- For loops -> iterate over arrays/maps, render body for each
- Nesting -> track indentation, apply to multi-line content
- Breakable spaces -> mark spaces as breakable (for Doc output)

Key functions:
- evaluate(template: &[TemplateNode], context: &TemplateContext) -> Result<String>
- resolve_variable(var: &VariableRef, context: &TemplateContext) -> TemplateValue
- render_value(value: &TemplateValue) -> String

For loop semantics:
- Array: iterate over elements, bind to variable name and 'it'
- Map: single iteration with map as context
- Other: single iteration with value

title: Implement conditional evaluation in evaluator

Implement conditional evaluation ($if(var)$...$else$...$endif$) in the template evaluator.

Tasks:
1. Evaluate truthiness of condition variable using existing is_truthy() method
2. Render the appropriate branch (then or else)
3. Support elseif chains by iterating through branches
4. Handle nested conditionals correctly

Truthiness rules (already implemented in TemplateValue::is_truthy):
- Any non-empty map is truthy
- Any array containing at least one truthy value is truthy
- Any non-empty string is truthy (even 'false')
- Boolean true is truthy
- Everything else is falsy

title: Implement for loop evaluation in evaluator
description:
Implement for loop evaluation ($for(var)$...$sep$...$endfor$) in the template evaluator.

Tasks:
1. Resolve the iteration variable from context
2. Handle different iteration modes:
   - Array: iterate over elements, bind to variable name AND 'it'
   - Map: single iteration with map as context
   - Other: single iteration with value
3. Create child context for each iteration with proper variable bindings
4. Render loop body for each iteration
5. Insert separator between iterations (not after last)
6. Handle nested loops correctly via context scoping

Per Pandoc semantics:
- Inside loop, can use either $variable$ or $it$ to refer to current element
- For nested access: $variable.field$ or $it.field$

title: Implement nesting/indentation in evaluator
description:
Implement nesting directive ($^$) for multi-line indentation in the template evaluator.

The nesting directive ensures subsequent lines are indented to line up with the first line.

Example:
  $item.number$  $^$$item.description$
produces:
  00123  A fine bottle of 18-year old
         Oban whiskey.

Tasks:
1. Track current column position during rendering
2. When encountering $^$, record current column as indentation level
3. For content after $^$, indent subsequent lines to this level
4. Handle nested nesting directives

Design consideration: The Haskell implementation uses Doc type with DL.nest for this. Our initial implementation can use a simpler approach by:
- Tracking indentation level as state
- Post-processing multi-line strings to add indentation

Note: Full fidelity with Pandoc's Doc-based approach may require future refactoring.
notes: See implementation plan: claude-notes/plans/pandoc-template-port/2025-11-24-evaluator-implementation-plan.md

title: Implement breakable spaces in evaluator
description:
Implement breakable space blocks ($~$...$~$) in the template evaluator.

Per Pandoc documentation:
'When rendering to a Doc, a distinction can be made between breakable and unbreakable spaces. Normally, spaces in the template itself are not breakable, but they can be made breakable in part of the template by using the ~ keyword.'

'The ~ keyword has no effect when rendering to Text or String.'

Tasks:
1. For String output (current approach): Simply render content as-is (spaces are not breakable)
2. If/when we implement Doc output: Mark spaces as breakable using DL.space equivalent

Design note: This feature is only meaningful when templates produce Doc output that can be reflowed. For simple String rendering, this is a no-op that just passes through content.

Priority: Lower than other evaluator tasks since it's effectively a no-op for String output.
notes: See implementation plan: claude-notes/plans/pandoc-template-port/2025-11-24-evaluator-implementation-plan.md

title: Implement template partials
description:
Implement partial (subtemplate) loading and evaluation for the template system.

Partials are subtemplates stored in different files that can be included via:
- Bare partial: $boilerplate()$
- Applied to variable: $date:fancy()$
- With separator: $articles:bibentry()[; ]$
- With pipes: $employee:name()/uppercase$

Key implementation requirements:
1. PartialResolver trait for abstracting file loading
2. Compile-time partial resolution (following Pandoc/doctemplates)
3. Path resolution (inherit template extension, same directory)
4. Recursion protection (max depth 50, return '(loop)')
5. Final newline stripping from partials
6. Array iteration for applied partials

Reference: jgm/doctemplates (Haskell implementation)
notes: Implementation plan: claude-notes/plans/pandoc-template-port/2025-11-25-partials-implementation-plan.md

3. **Rich source locations**: File/line/column for IDE integration
4. **Structured messages**: Tidyverse-style errors (problem, details, hints)

Key changes:
- Create EvalContext struct (variables + DiagnosticCollector + state)
- Update all evaluate_* functions to take &mut EvalContext
- Add render_with_diagnostics() API
- Use Q-9-* error codes for template subsystem

This should be completed before implementing partials (k-394) since partials need good error reporting for:
- Partial not found (Q-9-001)
- Partial parse errors (Q-9-002)
- Recursion limit exceeded (Q-9-003)

Add plain-text writer module to quarto-markdown-pandoc
description: Create writers/plaintext.rs that renders Pandoc AST (Inlines, Blocks) to pure plain text without HTML escaping. This is needed for deriving template values like pagetitle, author-meta, date-meta from MetaInlines. Unlike write_inlines_as_text in html.rs, this should NOT escape HTML entities. Plan: claude-notes/analysis/2025-11-25-plain-text-writer-design.md
design:
## RawInline/RawBlock
- Echo contents if format is 'plaintext', otherwise drop with warning

## PlainTextWriterContext
- Thread error diagnostics through all write functions
- Convenience functions return (String, Vec<DiagnosticMessage>)

## Inlines - Strip structure, keep content:
- Str, Space, SoftBreak, LineBreak: output directly
- Emph, Strong, Underline, Strikeout, Superscript, Subscript, SmallCaps, Span: recurse (no markers)
- Quoted: use actual quote characters
- Code: mimic markdown (backticks)
- Math: output raw TeX
- Link, Image: recurse into content only (no \![], [])
- Cite: recurse into content
- Insert, Delete, Highlight, EditComment: recurse
- Note: skip (no warning)
- RawInline: echo if 'plaintext', else drop with warning
- Shortcode, NoteReference, Attr: drop with warning

## Blocks - Mimic markdown writer:
- Plain, Paragraph, Header: write inlines
- CodeBlock: fenced with backticks
- BlockQuote: > prefix
- LineBlock: | prefix
- OrderedList: 1. 2. 3.
- BulletList: - prefix
- HorizontalRule: ---
- Div, Figure: write contents only
- RawBlock: echo if 'plaintext', else drop with warning

## Blocks - Drop with warning:
- DefinitionList, Table: complex structure
- BlockMetadata, NoteDefinitionPara, NoteDefinitionFencedBlock, CaptionBlock: Quarto extensions
notes:
Design decisions:
1. RawInline/RawBlock: echo contents if format is 'plaintext', otherwise drop with warning
2. Add PlainTextWriterContext for threading error diagnostics
3. Issue diagnostic warnings on dropped nodes:
   - RawInline/RawBlock with mismatched formats (not 'plaintext')
   - Unsupported Quarto extensions: Shortcode, NoteReference, Attr (inlines), BlockMetadata, NoteDefinitionPara, NoteDefinitionFencedBlock, CaptionBlock (blocks)
4. No HTML escaping (unlike write_inlines_as_text in html.rs)

title: Extensible filters for quarto-markdown-pandoc
description:
Implement extensible filter infrastructure allowing third-party filters to transform the Pandoc AST. This epic covers:

1. JSON filters - External processes that read/write JSON AST (Pandoc-compatible protocol)
2. Lua filters - Embedded Lua interpreter with direct AST access (mlua-based)

This provides compatibility with Pandoc's filter ecosystem while enabling performant Lua filters.

Design plans:
- JSON filters: claude-notes/plans/2025-11-26-json-filters-design.md
- Lua filters: claude-notes/plans/2025-11-26-lua-filters-design.md

title: JSON filter support for quarto-markdown-pandoc
description:
Implement JSON filter support following Pandoc's protocol:

**Protocol:**
- Stdin: Pandoc AST as JSON (using existing JSON writer)
- Stdout: Modified Pandoc AST as JSON (using existing JSON reader)
- Args: [target_format, ...]
- Environment: PANDOC_VERSION, PANDOC_READER_OPTIONS

**Implementation Tasks:**
1. Add --filter CLI argument to accept filter paths
2. Create filter execution infrastructure (spawn subprocess, pipe JSON)
3. Implement interpreter detection for .py, .hs, .pl, .rb, .php, .js, .r files
4. Add filter discovery (direct path, data dir, PATH)
5. Support multiple filters with sequential composition
6. Error handling (filter not found, non-zero exit, JSON parse errors)

**Files to modify:**
- crates/quarto-markdown-pandoc/src/main.rs (CLI args)
- crates/quarto-markdown-pandoc/src/filters/ (new module)

**Design plan:** claude-notes/plans/2025-11-26-json-filters-design.md

title: Lua filter support for quarto-markdown-pandoc
description:
Implement embedded Lua filter support using mlua:

**Architecture:**
- Use mlua crate for Rust-Lua integration
- Expose Pandoc AST types as Lua UserData
- Support both 'typewise' and 'topdown' traversal modes
- Provide pandoc.* namespace for element constructors

**Implementation Tasks:**
1. Add mlua dependency to Cargo.toml
2. Create Lua marshaling layer (Rust AST <-> Lua)
   - Pushers: Block, Inline, Meta types -> Lua tables/userdata
   - Peekers: Lua values -> Rust AST types
3. Implement element constructors (Str, Para, Header, etc.)
4. Create filter execution engine
   - Load filter script
   - Detect filter structure (explicit return vs global functions)
   - Apply traversal (typewise or topdown)
5. Add --lua-filter CLI argument
6. Implement return value semantics (nil=unchanged, element=replace, list=splice)
7. Expose global variables (FORMAT, PANDOC_VERSION, etc.)

**Key Design Decisions:**
- Start with minimal pandoc.* namespace (constructors only)
- Defer pandoc.utils, pandoc.text, etc. to later phases
- Use UserData for complex types vs tables for simple ones

**Files to create/modify:**
- crates/quarto-markdown-pandoc/Cargo.toml (add mlua)
- crates/quarto-markdown-pandoc/src/lua/ (new module)
- crates/quarto-markdown-pandoc/src/main.rs (CLI)

**Design plan:** claude-notes/plans/2025-11-26-lua-filters-design.md
notes:
Analysis and plan documents:
- mlua implementation analysis: claude-notes/plans/2025-12-02-mlua-analysis.md
- Filter diagnostics analysis: claude-notes/plans/2025-12-02-filter-diagnostics-analysis.md
- FilterContext refactoring: claude-notes/plans/2025-12-02-filter-context-refactoring.md
- Original design: claude-notes/plans/2025-11-26-lua-filters-design.md
- Lua globals reference: claude-notes/lua-globals-report.md

Implementation phases (all required):
- k-469: Phase 1 - Core types and infrastructure
- k-470: Phase 2 - Complete element coverage
- k-471: Phase 3 - Methods and traversal (includes walk())
- k-472: Phase 4 - Diagnostics and utilities (includes provenance tracking)

Key decisions (2025-12-02):

title: Investigate ASTContext serialization for JSON readers/writers
description: Currently ASTContext.with_filename() stores filename in both 'filenames' Vec and 'source_context', requiring a clone. This duplication exists during the migration period. Investigate how to serialize ASTContext properly in JSON readers/writers so we can eventually remove one of these storage locations and eliminate the clone.
notes:
IMPORTANT: This is related to broader SourceInfo serialization concerns. When we serialize SourceInfo structures with Rc<SourceInfo> parent chains, the serialization duplicates the entire parent chain for each nested element (serde doesn't deduplicate Rc references). This creates significant JSON size blowup with deeply nested structures.

After completing k-49 and k-50 (which will let us observe the serialization blowup in practice), we should investigate:
1. Whether ASTContext serialization has similar issues
2. If we need a custom serialization strategy for SourceInfo to avoid duplication
3. Whether we can use some form of reference/ID system in the JSON format

See claude-notes/rc-serialization-caveat-analysis.md for background.

title: Performance: Optimize SourceMapping to use Rc/Arc instead of Box
description: SourceMapping currently uses Box<SourceInfo> for parent references, causing expensive deep clones every time make_source_info() is called during YAML parsing (hundreds of times per document). Consider changing to Rc<SourceInfo> or Arc<SourceInfo> to make cloning cheap (reference counting). Need to study: serialization implications, thread-safety requirements, and performance benchmarks.
notes:
RECOMMENDATION: Use Rc<SourceInfo> instead of Box<SourceInfo>.

Analysis in claude-notes/sourcemapping-rc-arc-analysis.md

Key findings:
- Serde supports Rc with 'rc' feature flag
- Serialization doesn't preserve sharing (acceptable)
- Rc preferred over Arc (no threading, faster)
- Expected 10-50x speedup for nested documents
- Easy migration to Arc if needed later

Implementation:
1. Add serde rc feature to Cargo.toml
2. Box<SourceInfo> → Rc<SourceInfo>
3. Box::new → Rc::new
4. Verify serialization tests pass

title: Investigate and optimize SourceInfo JSON serialization size
description:
SourceInfo serialization duplicates parent chains in JSON. For a document with 100 YAML nodes sharing a parent, JSON contains ~100 full copies of the parent chain.

Problem: When shipping SourceInfo across WASM/TypeScript boundaries, large documents may produce bloated JSON.

Investigation needed:
1. Benchmark actual serialization sizes on real documents
2. Measure impact of gzip/brotli compression
3. Consider custom serialization with ID-based references
4. Evaluate flattening parent chains to original positions

See claude-notes/rc-serialization-caveat-analysis.md for detailed analysis.

Note: This is separate from the Rc optimization (k-43). Rc improves memory during parsing. This issue is about JSON size for process boundaries.

notes:
Design document: claude-notes/plans/2025-12-03-lua-runtime-abstraction-layer.md

## Key Design Decisions

Modeled after Deno's permission system (https://docs.deno.com/runtime/fundamentals/security/):

### SecurityPolicy Structure (Deno-aligned)
- `allow_read` / `deny_read` - File read paths (like --allow-read)
- `allow_write` / `deny_write` - File write paths (like --allow-write)
- `allow_net` / `deny_net` - Network hosts (like --allow-net)
- `allow_run` / `deny_run` - Programs to execute (like --allow-run)
- `allow_env` / `deny_env` - Environment variables (like --allow-env)
- `allow_cwd` - CWD operations (grouped with env, like Deno's chdir)
- `allow_sys` - System info APIs (like --allow-sys)

### Resolved Design Questions
1. **CWD handling**: Part of 'env' category; allow in native, deny in WASM, flag in sandboxed
2. **Async network**: Design for blocking now, note async as future consideration
3. **Module loading**: `require()` subject to file read permissions
4. **Error messages**: Detailed, actionable messages (Deno pattern)

### Key Patterns
- Deny takes precedence over allow (Deno pattern)
- Path wildcards supported (like `/home/user/*`)
- Env var suffix wildcards (like `AWS_*`)
- Replace Lua io/os modules with runtime-controlled versions

### Industry Research
- Deno: Mature model, full adoption of their patterns
- Node.js: Permission model in v23.5+, simpler than Deno
- Bun: No permission model yet (open issue #6617)

title: Investigate Lua filter traversal order (typewise multi-pass)
description:
Our current Lua filter implementation uses a single bottom-up pass, but Pandoc's typewise traversal does multiple passes:

1. First pass: ALL inline elements (Str, Emph, etc. + Inline fallback)
2. Then: Inlines list filter
3. Second pass: ALL block elements (Para, Header, etc. + Block fallback)
4. Then: Blocks list filter
5. Finally: Meta, then Pandoc

**Current behavior (filter.rs):**
- For each block, we process its inline children, then the block itself
- This is bottom-up within a single traversal

**Pandoc behavior (documented):**
- "Lua filter functions are run in the order: Inlines → Blocks → Meta → Pandoc"
- This suggests multiple passes over the document

**Tasks:**
1. Study Pandoc's Haskell source to understand exact traversal semantics
2. Write test cases comparing our output to Pandoc's for filters that depend on traversal order
3. Determine if the difference matters in practice
4. If needed, implement multi-pass traversal to match Pandoc

**Key files:**
- crates/quarto-markdown-pandoc/src/lua/filter.rs (apply_filter_to_block, apply_filter_to_inlines)
- crates/quarto-markdown-pandoc/src/lua/types.rs (walk_blocks_with_filter, walk_inlines_with_filter)

**Also verify:**

- Add tests for these behaviors

title: quarto.warn/error element location doesn't work for original document elements
description:
## Problem

The `quarto.warn(msg, elem)` and `quarto.error(msg, elem)` functions accept an optional AST element to attach source location information. However, this only works for elements **created by filters** (which have `FilterProvenance` source info), not elements **from the original document** (which have `SourceInfo::Original`).

This is a significant limitation because user-provided filters that want to act as linters cannot report warnings/errors about specific locations in the source document - they can only report the filter's own location.

## Root Cause

In `src/lua/diagnostics.rs`, the `source_info_to_path_line` function (lines 208-218) only handles `FilterProvenance`:

```rust
fn source_info_to_path_line(source_info: &SourceInfo) -> Option<(String, i64)> {
    match source_info {
        SourceInfo::FilterProvenance { filter_path, line } => {
            Some((filter_path.clone(), *line as i64))
        }
        // For Original source info, we don't have easy access to the filename
        // without a SourceContext. For now, return None to fall back to stack.
        _ => None,
    }
}
```

For `SourceInfo::Original`, we need access to `SourceContext` to:
1. Look up the `FileId` to get the filename
2. Map byte offsets to line/column numbers

The `SourceContext` is available in `ASTContext` but is not currently passed to the Lua diagnostic functions.

## How to Test

Create a test filter `linter.lua`:
```lua
function Str(elem)
    if elem.text:match('TODO') then
        quarto.warn('Found TODO in document', elem)
    end
    return elem
end
```

Create a test document `test.qmd`:
```markdown
This has a TODO item.
```

Run:
```bash
cargo run -- -L linter.lua -i test.qmd -t native
```

**Expected**: Warning shows location in `test.qmd` (line 1, around column 12)
**Actual**: Warning shows location in `linter.lua` (line 3, the quarto.warn call)

## Potential Solutions

1. **Pass ASTContext to Lua state**: Store `ASTContext` (or at least `SourceContext`) in the Lua registry so diagnostic functions can access it
2. **Thread-local context**: Use a thread-local to store context during filter execution
3. **Closure capture**: Capture context in the Lua function closures created in `register_quarto_namespace`

Option 1 or 3 seems cleanest. The context would need to be set before filter execution and cleared after.

## Related

- Parent issue: k-480 (Implement quarto.warn/error Lua functions)
- Plan: claude-notes/plans/2025-12-03-lua-filter-diagnostics-implementation.md
- Discussion: Element location extraction was identified as incomplete during implementation review
notes:
Plan document: claude-notes/plans/2025-12-03-k481-source-location-resolution.md

FINAL APPROACH: Store SourceInfo as Lua table (not userdata)

Why not userdata?
- In Pandoc, userdata = AST nodes. Filters may use type(x)=='userdata' to identify elements.
- Using userdata for non-AST data could cause Pandoc compatibility issues.

Why not thread-local IDs?  
- If diagnostic entries are serialized, IDs become meaningless.

Solution: Serialize SourceInfo to plain Lua table, deserialize on extraction.

Lua table format:
  { t = 'Original', file_id = 0, start_offset = 42, end_offset = 55 }
  { t = 'Substring', parent = {...}, start_offset = 10, end_offset = 20 }
  { t = 'FilterProvenance', filter_path = '...', line = 42 }

Changes needed in diagnostics.rs:
1. Add source_info_to_lua_table() and source_info_from_lua_table()
2. Update add_diagnostic() to store serialized SourceInfo
3. Update extract_lua_diagnostics() to deserialize and pass to builder
4. Remove obsolete resolution functions

Benefits:
- No SourceContext needed in Lua
- Pure Lua tables (Pandoc-compatible)
- Serialization-safe
- Resolution stays in Rust

There are 43 instances of SourceInfo::default() across the codebase where we're not tracking source locations. Many of these could and should track actual source information from tree-sitter nodes or other sources.

Affected files:
- src/readers/json.rs
- src/readers/qmd.rs  
- src/pandoc/treesitter.rs (3 instances)
- src/pandoc/treesitter_utils/document.rs
- src/pandoc/treesitter_utils/postprocess.rs
- src/pandoc/block.rs
- src/pandoc/inline.rs
- src/pandoc/meta.rs

Tasks:
1. Audit each SourceInfo::default() instance to determine:
   - Is source location information available from tree-sitter node?
   - Is this data derived from existing AST with source info?
   - Is this a legitimate case where no source info exists (e.g., synthetic nodes)?

2. Categorize instances:
   - Can be fixed: node available, should track location
   - Should propagate: derived from existing AST, should copy/combine source info
   - Legitimate default: synthetic/generated content with no source

3. Create systematic plan to fix trackable instances

4. Fix instances file by file, verifying with tests

5. Document remaining legitimate default() uses with comments explaining why

Expected outcome:
- Maximum source location tracking throughout AST
- Better error messages and diagnostics
- Clear documentation for cases where default() is appropriate

description:

title: Property testing framework for CommonMark subset validation
description: Design and implement a property testing framework using proptest to verify that generated Pandoc ASTs roundtrip correctly through qmd writer → qmd reader and comrak parser. This provides stronger coverage than hand-written differential tests by generating arbitrary valid inputs.
notes:
See claude-notes/plans/2025-12-16-property-testing-commonmark-subset.md for full design.

APPROACH: Feature set-based generators that progressively add complexity.

FEATURE SET DESIGN:
- Generator takes a set of enabled features (InlineFeatures, BlockFeatures)
- When using a feature (e.g., Emph), recurse with that feature removed
- Elegantly prevents Emph-inside-Emph and naturally limits nesting depth
- Enables progressive complexity testing

INLINE PROGRESSION (L0-L7):
L0: Plain text (Str, Space, SoftBreak)
L1: + Emph
L2: + Strong
L3: + Code
L4: + Link
L5: + Image
L6: + Autolink
L7: + LineBreak

BLOCK PROGRESSION (B0-B6):
B0: Paragraph only
B1: + Header
B2: + CodeBlock
B3: + HorizontalRule
B4: + BlockQuote (recursive)
B5: + BulletList (recursive)
B6: + OrderedList

IMPLEMENTATION: 7 phases with checkpoints after each level
- Each phase adds features and verifies tests pass before proceeding
- Progressive approach helps isolate which features cause failures

NORMALIZATION:
- Strip heading IDs
- Figure → Paragraph(Image)
- Strip autolink uri class
- Strip extra code block attributes

title: Filesystem synchronization design for quarto-hub
description:
Design the bidirectional synchronization between filesystem (.qmd files) and automerge documents.

## Core Design: Unified Sync Algorithm

A single fork-and-merge algorithm handles ALL sync scenarios (startup, shutdown, periodic, user-triggered):

1. Fork doc at last sync checkpoint
2. Apply filesystem content to fork via update_text (Myers diff)
3. Merge fork back into main doc (CRDT merge)
4. Write merged result to filesystem
5. Update checkpoint

This naturally handles: no changes (no-op), automerge-only changes, filesystem-only changes, and true divergence (three-way merge).

## Key Decisions
- Automerge update_text handles diffing internally (grapheme-aware Myers)
- Sync state stored locally in sync-state.json (not synced to peers)
- Algorithm converges: after sync, fs and automerge match

## Related Issues
- k-r2t1 (filesystem serialization strategy)
- k-yvfo (conflict resolution for divergence)

Design document: claude-notes/plans/2025-12-09-filesystem-sync-design.md

title: Audit anyhow::anyhow\! usages for error structure loss
description:
Several places in the codebase use anyhow::anyhow\!() in ways that lose structured error information. This issue tracks reviewing and potentially fixing these patterns.

## Problematic Patterns Found

### qmd-syntax-helper crate

1. **syntax_check.rs:89** - Joins error strings and wraps in anyhow:
   ```rust
   let error_msg = errors.join("\n");
   Err(anyhow::anyhow\!("{}", error_msg))
   ```

2. **grid_tables.rs:137** - Uses debug format on diagnostics:
   ```rust
   anyhow::anyhow\!("Failed to write markdown output: {:?}", diagnostics)
   ```

3. **definition_lists.rs:190** - Same issue as grid_tables.rs

### validate-yaml crate

- Uses anyhow for simple CLI errors, likely acceptable for a validation tool.

## Recommended Actions

1. For qmd-syntax-helper: Consider using proper diagnostic rendering with `to_text()` instead of debug format
2. Review if these tools need the same rich error display as the main CLI
3. Consider creating a shared error display utility

## Notes

- Simple IO/path errors using anyhow are acceptable
- The main render.rs:201 issue was fixed separately (handled parse errors specially to avoid duplicate 'Error:' prefix)

Root cause: The system passes full document content from Automerge to Monaco on every remote change. Monaco has no knowledge of what changed or where, so it cannot preserve cursor position.

title: Design structural hash-based AST reconciliation algorithm
description:
Design a reconciliation algorithm for PandocAST nodes inspired by React 15's reconciliation. Use structural hashes as virtual keys for node identity since we don't have explicit id keys. The hash of a node = hash(type, content, children_hashes), excluding source locations. This enables O(n) reconciliation with efficient subtree skipping when hashes match.

Approach:
- Compute structural hashes for both pre-engine and post-engine ASTs
- Hash serves as 'virtual key' for matching nodes across ASTs
- If hashes match, subtrees are identical - transfer source locations wholesale
- If hashes differ but types match, recurse into children
- Use hash-based alignment for children lists (hash -> node multimap)

Plan: claude-notes/plans/2025-12-17-structural-hash-reconciliation-design.md
